results.title: FDA targets WHO Listed Authority status as it marks 30th anniversary
results.content: The Food and Drugs Authority (FDA) is working towards attaining World Health Organisation (WHO) Listed Authority status as part of efforts to strengthen Ghana’s position in global health regulation. Chief Executive Officer of the FDA, Professor Kwabena Frimpong-Manso Opuni, announced the ambition at the launch of the Authority’s 30th anniversary celebrations in Accra on Tuesday, November 24, 2026. He said the Authority was taking steps to secure the recognition, which would further strengthen its standing among regulatory institutions meeting internationally recognised standards. “Our ambition is not simply to be an effective national regulator, but to be a trusted regulatory partner and a centre of excellence that contributes meaningfully to public health protection across Africa,” he said.

results.title: Government assures Food and Drugs Authority of technical independence and support
results.content: The government has assured the Food and Drugs Authority (FDA) of its commitment to protecting the institution’s technical independence, saying its regulatory decisions must remain free from external interference. Chief Director of the Ministry of Health, Desmond Boateng, gave the assurance on behalf of Health Minister Kwabena Mintah Akandoh at the launch of the FDA’s 30th anniversary celebrations. He said government would provide the Authority with the support and resources needed to strengthen its regulatory capacity. Mr Boateng said the FDA’s independence was essential to ensuring that decisions on the safety and quality of regulated products were guided by scientific evidence, public safety and the national interest. “As a government, we guarantee the FDA absolute technical independence in this endeavour. results.title: Qualified but unemployed: who is responsible?
results.content: According to the Ghana Statistical Service, unemployment among young people aged 15 to 35 averaged 21.9% during the first three quarters of 2025, compared with a national rate of 12.8%. Among those aged 15 to 24, unemployment averaged 32.4%. These figures cover young people generally, not university graduates alone, but they provide context for the labour market graduates are entering.
